checkpoints.description: Task 'integrate-aikit' completed successfully.

[1/4] mechanical: rewrite eslint.config.js as a flat config for the installed ESLint 8.57 (legacy CJS config under type:module could never load) and fix the lint script, then repair resize_sprites.py open(); [2/4] hygiene: resolve the three external font URLs in index.html and the absolute machine paths in the two generate scripts; [3/4] typecheck and build: fix the TestingHarness event handlers, its nullable AISystem, helpers.pick's generic bound and the untyped config reads in tests/core.test.ts; [4/4] rerun aikit check to 7/7, record the checklist outcome, then commit .aikit/, .gitignore and the fixed files explicitly

impact_assessment.why: the integration check left 5 of 7 gates red and a project commits only when every gate passes (PRINCIPLE-011 R8), so these fixes unblock the first verified commit of MemoryReconstruction
impact_assessment.benefits: gates become real rather than declared: lint actually loads a config, typecheck and build pin the types, hygiene keeps the tree portable and offline-clean, README gains the cold-start contract
impact_assessment.risks: contract: fixes must not change game behaviour or weaken any test assertion; dependency: no new packages, the flat config uses packages already installed; concurrency: the user's other uncommitted asset work is never staged or edited; state: .aikit memory stays uncommitted until the final green run
impact_assessment.mitigation: run npm test after every milestone and the full aikit check at the end; typing fixes only cast or constrain, assertions stay untouched; if lint under the declared strictness produces a flood of findings, stop and bring the options to the user instead of weakening the config unilaterally

checkpoints.description: checklists: passed; all 7/7 gates green (test, lint, typecheck, build, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); resolved ESLint flat config, typing errors, build minifier, hygiene paths/font annotations, and README quick reference
Task 'green-gates' completed successfully.

checklists: passed; all 7/7 gates green (test, lint, typecheck, build, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); generated the Memory Light sprite/tileset/background set, added atlas metadata, integrated textured tiles, actors, camera and HUD, and applied review fixes

impact_assessment.why: the game shipped placeholder graph art and no runtime actor rendering, so the visual layer did not represent the Memory Reconstruction theme
impact_assessment.benefits: coherent themed art direction, animated player and enemies, biome tile atlases, parallax backdrops, themed HUD, and a reproducible generator wired to npm
impact_assessment.risks: contract: asset paths and atlas metadata must match the runtime; dependency: Pillow is only needed to regenerate art, not to run or build; concurrency: existing uncommitted user work stays untouched; state: generated binaries increase repository size but remain deterministic
impact_assessment.mitigation: sprite_atlas is validated by tests, build copies assets into dist, and headless runtime checks confirm centered camera, pinned HUD, actors and zero failed requests

checkpoints.description: Task 'memory-light-art' completed successfully.
[1/1] add the tracked LICENSE file to the README tree, rerun the 7 project gates, and commit the doc fix

impact_assessment.why: the AGPL-3.0 license commit added LICENSE but left README.md's tree incomplete, so the guidelines gate now fails and a cold-starting agent sees a tree that disagrees with the repository
impact_assessment.benefits: README and tracked files agree again; the project's Phase 4 gate returns to 7/7 so the next feature starts from a green baseline
impact_assessment.risks: contract: documentation only, no code or behavior change; dependency: none; concurrency: none, no other writer is touching README; state: none, only the README line changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: verify the tree against git ls-files, rerun python aikit.py check MemoryReconstruction to 7/7, then stage README.md alone and commit it

checkpoints.description: checklists: passed; 7/7 gates green (test, lint, typecheck, build, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); README tree now lists the tracked LICENSE file
Task 'readme-license-tree' completed successfully.

[1/1] move the four stale untracked scaffold files to a timestamped temp backup, remove the dangling performance-guidelines reference, regenerate the codebase map, rerun the 7 gates, commit the docs, then strict-verify and push

impact_assessment.why: four untracked files from the initial Stellar Drift scaffold block check --strict, and docs/Graphics.md and .aikit/codebase_map.md point at them even though they are not part of the delivery
impact_assessment.benefits: the project tree becomes clean and delivery-ready, the pending README/LICENSE commit can be verified and pushed, and the docs and AST map stop referencing a broken Python benchmark that belongs to another prototype
impact_assessment.risks: contract: documentation and generated map only, no runtime or gameplay behaviour changes; dependency: none; concurrency: the untracked files may be user work, so they are moved to a timestamped temp backup instead of deleted; state: none beyond the generated map and ledger
impact_assessment.mitigation: back up all four paths before touching them, grep every reference, rerun python aikit.py check MemoryReconstruction to 7/7, then stage only the tracked docs and map

checkpoints.description: checklists: passed; 7/7 gates green (test, lint, typecheck, build, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); four stale untracked scaffold paths moved to a temp backup, the dangling performance-guidelines reference removed, and the codebase map regenerated
Task 'cleanup-stale-scaffolding' completed successfully.

[1/4] progression contract: add gameplay.progression.fragments and abilityUnlocks config, handle player:addMemory in PlayerSystem (fragments -> XP -> level -> ability unlock), and write failing-first tests; [2/4] world collectibles: MemoryFragmentSystem with deterministic chunk spawns, pickup radius, bob animation, collected-set persistence, main.ts registration, and tests; [3/4] presentation and docs: HUD fragment counter and level, README/architecture/graphics updates, ADR-003; [4/4] run all 7 gates, record the checklist, commit, strict-verify and push

impact_assessment.why: the game already spawns memoryFragment entities and awards memoryValue on kills, but nothing collects world fragments, nothing listens to player:addMemory, the HUD never shows fragments or level, and the progression data is therefore dead state
impact_assessment.benefits: the core Memory Reconstruction loop becomes playable: explore, collect glowing fragments, earn XP, level up, unlock heal/shield/ultimate, and see progress in the HUD; the loop is deterministic, serializable, and tested
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new config keys and a new module, existing PlayerSystem API unchanged; dependency: no new packages, PixiJS and Vitest already declared; concurrency: no parallel writer, the tree is clean at start; state: new collected-fragment state is serialized in the new module and PlayerSystem progression remains backward compatible
impact_assessment.mitigation: write unit tests first for fragment XP, negative amounts, level-up unlocks, chunk spawn extraction and pickup distance; keep PIXI rendering out of the pure helpers; run npm test after each milestone and the full 7-gate check before committing

checkpoints.description: checklists: passed; 7/7 project gates green (test, lint, typecheck, build, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); added the configurable fragment XP/ability-unlock contract, MemoryFragmentSystem with deterministic ids, pickup radius, bob animation and serialized collected set, HUD fragment/level display, world spawn entries in every biome, cached-chunk reload so fragments and tiles return after streaming out, and failing-first tests for progression, helpers, persistence and chunk streaming
Task 'memory-fragment-loop' completed successfully.

[1/3] intent contract: add combat:attack and combat:damage events, make PlayerSystem emit slash/ultimate attack intents with sourceId, radius, base damage and crit flag, and add failing-first PlayerSystem tests; [2/3] resolution: CombatSystem handles attack intents with radial hit detection, applies crit once, emits combat:damage separately from combat:hit, and awards XP/memory on player kills, with failing-first tests for in-range, out-of-range and crit; [3/3] update the architecture/ADR, run the 7 gates, record checklists passed, commit, strict-verify and push

impact_assessment.why: PlayerSystem emits combat:hit for melee with no targetId or sourceId, so CombatSystem's onHit cannot resolve it; enemies never take player melee damage and the existing combat-kill player:addMemory reward path never fires
impact_assessment.benefits: player slash and ultimate become real damage sources, kills award XP and memory fragments, the fragment loop gains its combat path, and the event contract cleanly separates attack intent from resolved damage
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new combat:attack/combat:damage events and PlayerSystem stops emitting combat:hit; CombatSystem keeps combat:hit as the targeted incoming-damage input; dependency: none added; concurrency: the tree is clean and no other writer is active; state: no persistent state changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: write the intent and resolution tests first, keep the existing enemy attack path on combat:hit, assert a single critical multiplier application, and run the full 7-gate check before committing

checkpoints.description: checklists: passed; 7/7 project gates green (test, lint, typecheck, build, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); decoupled combat attack intents from resolved damage with combat:attack and combat:damage events, implemented radial melee hit detection with single crit and knockback in CombatSystem, updated PlayerSystem slash and ultimate attack emitters, updated architecture docs and ADR-004, refreshed codebase map, and added unit tests for attack intent generation, distance gating, crit multiplier, and enemy-to-player hits
Task 'player-melee-resolution' completed successfully.

[1/3] add start script to package.json, create start.bat and start.sh with node/npm checks; [2/3] update README quick start and tree, record ADR-005; [3/3] run all 7 gates, record checklist, commit, strict-verify and push

impact_assessment.why: launching the game currently requires manual cd and npm run dev; double-clicking index.html fails on file:// CORS, and npm start fails with missing script
impact_assessment.benefits: zero-friction startup via start.bat, start.sh, and standard npm start, with automated node presence checks and dependency fallback
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing scripts intact, only start alias added; dependency: none added; concurrency: clean tree; state: no state changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: verify script paths and execution, update README tree for guidelines gate, and run full 7-gate suite
